idea-plugin.name: Claude Code Chat
idea-plugin.description:
Claude Code for IntelliJ

Bring the full power of Claude Code directly into your IDE. Chat with Claude in a side panel, edit code inline with natural-language instructions, fix errors with one click in the Alt+Enter menu, generate commit messages from your staged diff, and let Claude read, edit, and create files in your project — all without leaving IntelliJ.

Inline AI Actions

  • Edit with Claude (Cmd+Alt+K / Ctrl+Alt+K, or the Claude icon in the floating code toolbar) — select code, describe a change in plain English, review the diff, and accept or reject.
  • Fix with Claude — Alt+Enter on any IDE-detected error or warning to get an AI-powered quick-fix that lives next to IntelliJ's own intentions.
  • Generate Commit Message — one click in the VCS commit dialog turns your staged diff into a Conventional Commits-style message.
  • Apply link on every chat code block — replace the selection in your active editor with the suggested code after a diff review.

Chat Panel

  • Multiple parallel Claude Code sessions in a side panel
  • Project-aware: Claude works in your open project's directory
  • Session memory: Claude remembers context across messages
  • Markdown rendering with syntax-highlighted code blocks
  • Tool-use indicators with colored status signals and diff summaries
  • File chips — drag/drop, copy/paste, or type a filename to attach files as context; resolves bare filenames against your project
  • Large-text paste chips — long pastes collapse into a compact chip; double-click to expand back into the input
  • Smart auto-scroll — follows new output unless you've scrolled up to read; "Jump to latest" button keeps you in control
  • Inline diffs: expandable old vs. new for every edit Claude makes, with consolidated stats per file
  • Clickable file links and a changed-files summary grouped by folder
  • Copy and re-edit buttons on messages and code blocks

Right-Click Context Menu

  • Explain — understand code, methods, files, or entire folders (recursive summaries)
  • Refactor — get suggestions for readability, performance, and best practices
  • Generate Tests — create unit tests for selected code, whole files, or every source file in a folder (14+ languages)
  • Fix — identify and fix bugs in selected code
  • Open Claude Session Here — right-click any folder to start a new session rooted there
  • Debug with Claude — right-click in the Run/Debug console to send exceptions, log flows, or output to Claude

Works from the editor, project tree, and Run/Debug console.

Productivity

  • Editable model selector: type any Claude model ID; remembers models seen in past sessions
  • Keyboard shortcuts: Cmd+Shift+I to toggle the chat panel, Cmd+Alt+K for inline edit (Ctrl variants on Windows/Linux)
  • Stop requests with Escape or double Ctrl+C / Cmd+C
  • Permission mode: acceptEdits (file edits OK, shell blocked), bypassPermissions (allow all), or plan (read-only) — maps to the CLI's --permission-mode
  • Project tree auto-refreshes when Claude creates, modifies, or deletes files
  • Cost tracking per response

Prerequisites

  • Install the Claude CLI: npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code (works on macOS, Linux, and Windows)
  • Authenticate by running claude in a terminal
  • Make sure the CLI is on your PATH so the plugin can spawn it. On Windows, npm typically installs claude.cmd under %APPDATA%\npm\ — that directory must be on PATH.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.0.4

  • Windows support — the CLI invocation no longer assumes the Unix script command for pty allocation; on Windows it spawns claude.cmd directly. Mac/Linux behaviour is unchanged. claude resolution layers three strategies because IntelliJ's JVM often inherits a PATH that's missing the user-PATH entries added by the Node.js MSI installer (where %APPDATA%\npm\ normally sits) — meaning a bare claude can be runnable from CMD/PowerShell yet invisible to the plugin: (1) where against the inherited PATH; (2) direct probes of %APPDATA%\npm, %LOCALAPPDATA%\npm, %ProgramFiles%\nodejs; (3) npm config get prefix. Prefers the .cmd extension over the Unix shell-script wrapper that npm also installs. The resolved binary's directory is also prepended to the spawned process's PATH so internal shell-outs from claude.cmd work. Settings → Claude CLI path accepts an absolute path as a manual fallback if auto-detection fails.
  • Permission modes (replaces auto-accept toggle) — Settings → Tools → Claude Code now exposes a permission-mode dropdown: acceptEdits (default, file edits go through, shell commands blocked), bypassPermissions (Claude can run any tool), or plan (read-only). Maps directly to the CLI's --permission-mode. The old binary "auto-accept" toggle pretended an interactive permission flow that the CLI's -p mode doesn't actually support; this replaces it with what the CLI really offers.
  • Permission-blocked hint — when Claude's reply looks like it's been blocked by your current permission mode (e.g. "Could you approve the Write tool…"), an inline hint appears with a clickable link straight to Settings to switch modes.
  • Edit with Claude in the floating toolbar — now for JS/TS too — the JavaScript/TypeScript plugin uses its own Floating.CodeToolbar.Web group separate from the generic one, so the Claude icon was missing on web files. Action now registers to both groups; the keyboard shortcut was unaffected.
  • Deprecated API fix — replaced ReadAction.compute(ThrowableComputable) with Application.runReadAction(Computable) in the chat-input filename resolver. Flagged by the JetBrains plugin verifier as deprecated and slated for removal in a future platform release. No behaviour change.

1.0.3

  • Edit with Claude — select code, hit Cmd+Alt+K / Ctrl+Alt+K (or click the Claude icon in the floating code toolbar, alongside Show Context Actions / Extract / Surround), then type a natural-language instruction. Claude returns the rewrite and a side-by-side diff opens; Accept replaces the selection, Reject discards it. Works in any editor regardless of language.
  • Apply button on chat code blocks — every fenced code block in the Claude chat now has an [apply] link next to [copy]. Select the target code in the active editor, click apply, review the diff, and accept to replace your selection in-place.
  • Generate Commit Message with Claude — new button in the VCS commit dialog toolbar. Reads git diff --cached (falls back to git diff), sends it to Claude, and fills the commit message field with a Conventional Commits-style result.
  • Fix with Claude quick-fix intention — Alt+Enter on any IDE-detected error or warning now offers "Fix with Claude". Sends the offending lines + the inspection message to Claude, shows a diff, applies on accept. Works for any language and any inspection (compiler errors, linter warnings, code-style issues).
  • Expandable paste chips — large-text paste chips can now be double-clicked to expand back into the input. Cursor changes to a pointer and a tooltip reminds you of the gesture; file chips remain non-expandable to keep their path semantics intact.
  • Inline code completion removed — the experimental opt-in was dropped after evaluation: with the CLI-based auth path, latency was 1.5-3s per suggestion vs. sub-200ms for purpose-built FIM models. Will revisit if Anthropic ships a low-latency endpoint.

1.0.2

  • Smart auto-scroll — chat output only follows new messages when you're already at the bottom; if you've scrolled up to read, your position is preserved. A floating "↓ Jump to latest" button appears in the bottom-right when you're scrolled away.
  • File chips in chat input — drag/drop, copy/paste, or paste a path and it becomes a compact 📎 filename chip that expands to the absolute path on submit. Click the ✕ to remove.
  • Smart filename resolution — pasting just a filename (with or without extension) resolves to the project file via FilenameIndex; on macOS, Finder copies are read from NSPasteboard via AppleScript when JBR's clipboard bridge only exposes the bare filename.
  • Large-text paste chips — pasting >250 chars or >3 lines creates a "Pasted #N · X lines" chip instead of cluttering the input. Submitted text uses the full content.
  • Open Claude Session Here — right-click any folder in the project tree to open a new Claude Code session rooted at that folder.
  • Editable model selector — type any model ID in Settings, not just the bundled list; recognized models from sessions are remembered. Adds Opus 4.7 to the bundled list.
  • Better diff summary — Edit results now show ~modified, +added, -removed with proper LCS-based counts instead of overcounting.
  • Tool-aware thinking indicator — shows the running tool name and elapsed seconds while Claude is working.
  • Tool window focus — Send-to-Claude actions now activate the Claude tool window (focusing the input) rather than just showing it.
  • Debug log off by default — checkbox starts unchecked so it doesn't take up space.

1.0.1

  • Explain Folder — right-click any folder in the project tree to get a hierarchical summary of its contents, with breakdowns for each sub-folder up to 2 levels deep
  • File-type agnostic explanations — Explain works on any file type (Dockerfile, YAML, Kubernetes manifests, build files, etc.), not just source code
  • Improved prompts — all right-click action prompts rewritten with structured output format, better guidance for test generation (matches project conventions), and concrete code in refactor/fix results
  • Settings crash fix — fixed a NullPointerException that occurred when opening Settings during plugin unload

1.0.0

  • Console integration — right-click in Run/Debug console to debug exceptions, explain log flows, or send output to Claude
  • Folder-level test generation — generate tests for all source files in a directory (supports 14+ languages)
  • Send to Claude — send selected code, files, or console output as context from any right-click menu
  • Interactive permission prompts — Allow/Deny buttons in the chat panel for Claude's file operations
  • Inline diffs — expandable diff viewers showing old vs. new code for every edit Claude makes
  • Edit consolidation — consecutive edits to the same file are grouped into a single entry with cumulative diffs
  • Thinking display — real-time indicator showing Claude's reasoning when extended thinking is active
  • Debug log panel — collapsible panel for inspecting internal session operations
  • Session auto-naming — sessions are automatically named based on the first message
  • Auto-accept permissions setting — configure whether file operations require manual approval
  • File deletion tracking — detects and displays files deleted via Bash commands
  • Model info in header — active model name shown in each response header

0.1.0

  • Initial release
  • Multi-session chat panel with Claude Code CLI
  • Right-click actions: Explain, Refactor, Generate Tests, Fix
  • Editor and project tree context menu integration
  • Markdown rendering with syntax highlighting
  • Clickable file links and changed files summary
  • Copy/edit buttons on messages and code blocks
  • Model selection and cost tracking
  • Welcome page with feature overview
